data.command: Describe T1046 Network Service Discovery scanning

data.text:
As a Linux system administrator, I can tell you that T1046 Network Service Discovery scanning is a reconnaissance technique used by attackers to gather information about the network services running on a target system.

To start with, I'm running a Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server with an nginx/1.24.0 web server listening on port 80 and a MySQL server running on a different host. I've also got a kernel 5.15.0-91, just in case you're wondering.

Now, when it comes to Network Service Discovery scanning, attackers can use various tools to identify open ports and services on a target system. Some common tools used for this are Nmap, Nessus, or OpenVAS. These tools can scan for services like HTTP (port 80), HTTPS (port 443), SSH (port 22), or MySQL (port 3306) among others.

Here's an example of an Nmap scan on a specific IP address:

```bash
nmap -sV -p 1-65535 -T4 192.0.2.1
```
